title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching + quant profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Adds autotune defaults for batching/caching, new quantization profile selection logic, and unit-economics reporting tooling for cost analysis. No breaking API changes.
body:
Context: Customers and internal benchmarks show that suboptimal defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching plus inconsistent quantization profiles are driving unnecessary per-token cost for many workloads. This PR bundles three related improvements: 1) autotune & sensible defaults for batching and cache TTL/size tuned per model/traffic profile, 2) quantization profile selector and safe fallbacks for model variants, and 3) unit-economics tooling: a lightweight endpoint + console surfaces per-route token cost, effective batching, and expected savings from suggested config changes.

Summary of changes: - new autotune service (services/autotune) that ingests sample traffic profiles and emits recommended defaults (batch_size, max_latency_target_ms, cache_ttl_secs, cache_size_entries) - runtime integration to apply recommended defaults on deploy + a gradual rollout path (canary -> scale) - quantization profile registry + selector (redwood-model-registry/quant_profiles) with compatibility checks and fallback rules when a profile would cause quality regressions - unit economics API (backend/api/uecon) that aggregates token counts, latency-adjusted cost, and model variant costs, plus endpoints used by console - console UI additions under redwood-console to show per-route UEcon and one-click apply suggestions - e2e integration tests and perf canary for a representative chat workload that validates latency and quality budgets

Checklist: - [x] Autotune service + API implemented - [x] Runtime hooks to receive/apply defaults - [x] Quant profiles added and compatibility heuristics - [x] Unit-econ API + console panels - [x] Integration tests + perf canary - [x] Docs: docs/cost-optimization/autotune.md and console release notes

Design notes: - Autotune runs in read-only mode by default; applying recommendations requires an operator approval flag or can be enabled via a per-org rollout policy. This avoids accidental regressions. - Quantization profiles are validated by running lightweight evals against representative prompts; if quality drift > threshold we keep a safer profile and surface the tradeoff. - Unit-econ tooling uses weighted token costs (infrastructure cost + amortized model spin-up) and shows expected monthly savings given traffic and suggested config.

Why packaged together: The three items are tightly coupled in practice: batching/caching defaults and quantization decisions are the primary levers for per-token/unit cost. Providing an autotune + tooling surface lets us recommend non-obvious, multi-dimensional changes and quantify their dollar impact for customers and SRE.

Notes for reviewers: Focus on correctness of the runtime hooks and safety of automatic rollout behavior. Pay attention to the quant profile fallback tests in tests/quant_compat_test.py. There is an optional feature flag (features.autotune.apply_recommendations) set to false by default.
